messages.content: You are a senior research synthesizer. Produce authoritative, grounded notes that synthesize the sources for the given research question. Structure the notes with ## (level-2) section headings, ending with a ## Open questions section naming evidence gaps and what would settle them. Cite every factual claim with an inline footnote marker using the FULL source ID exactly as given in Sources, e.g. "RAG grounds generation in retrieved passages [^openalex:W123]." At the end, add one definition line per cited source, e.g. "[^openalex:W123]: Paper Title Here. Labs preprint servers (arXiv, bioRxiv) are primary; journals are primary; aggregators are secondary — say which is which. Every section MUST cite at least two sources; a section with no citations is a failure. Never shorten or invent source IDs, never use bare [Title] brackets, never use (Author, Year) style. When sources cite each other (see 'cited in-set by'), say so: agreement across independent sources is stronger evidence. Cover every distinct option the sources support — competing approaches, vendors, and providers each get their own treatment with head-to-head trade-offs, never just the most popular one. End with a ## Practical takeaways section: concrete recommendations (use X when Y), trade-offs, and what to try first — every recommendation grounded in a cited source.

## Open questions section

* What are the precise technical architectures, embedding mechanisms, and generation workflows of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in modern large language models, given that the provided sources failed to return substantive technical literature due to automated security verification pages [^crossref:10.1515/9783112226780-009, ^crossref:10.36227/techrxiv.177272838.89432844/v1, ^crossref:10.5040/bci-0kgi.ch-1]? 
* What would settle these evidence gaps is a complete retrieval of academic research papers, preprint texts, or technical documentation detailing RAG pipelines, rather than HTTP security challenge responses and login error pages [^crossref:10.1515/9783112226780-009, ^crossref:10.36227/techrxiv.177272838.89432844/v1, ^crossref:10.5040/bci-0kgi.ch-1].

## Practical takeaways section

* Given the lack of valid technical sources, no concrete implementation recommendations, vendor comparisons, or workflow trade-offs can be reliably grounded in the provided set [^crossref:10.1515/9783112226780-009, ^crossref:10.36227/techrxiv.177272838.89432844/v1, ^crossref:10.5040/bci-0kgi.ch-1].
* To bypass bot protection blocks and error screens, ensure that input sources link directly to accessible document text rather than security verification portals or authentication walls [^crossref:10.1515/9783112226780-009, ^crossref:10.36227/techrxiv.177272838.89432844/v1, ^crossref:10.5040/bci-0kgi.ch-1].

[^crossref:10.1515/9783112226780-009]: Human Verification / Temporary error. Academic publisher book chapter index (secondary/aggregator content blocked by bot protection).
[^crossref:10.36227/techrxiv.177272838.89432844/v1]: TechRxiv preprint repository security verification page (primary preprint server blocked by bot protection).
[^crossref:10.5040/bci-0kgi.ch-1]: Bloomsbury Collections login and error page interface text (secondary academic book platform).
